host_timing_note: Measured on the FreeRTOS POSIX port, where every task is a thread of a Linux process. Times, jitter and latencies are those of the host's scheduler and are not what the same code shows on a microcontroller; counts, orderings and sizes of protocol data are independent of the host. The trace's and the observer's times are CLOCK_MONOTONIC of the same Linux VM; a task's release, start and running time are the kernel's decisions inside vTaskSwitchContext() and the tick handler, which on this port run in host threads: the figures include the host's delivery of the tick and of thread wake-ups. The execution times and CPU shares are x86-64 times of a host thread and say nothing about a Cortex-M3; the stack depths are those of host threads with x86-64 frames. Counts (jobs, frames, gaps) are independent of the host.

tick_lead.stretch: consecutive counts each first seen before its tick was due, from the first sight of the first to the due time of the last; the trace sees the count only at a SWITCH or READY event, so a stretch begins at a sight, which can be after the count got ahead

process.arrival: the arrival of the sensor job whose sample released it
